pivotFrame: standing world frame; the body origin motion is rotated about a registered point shifted by d, which adds the angle-dependent translation (I - R(f)) d
cost: summed femur-to-tibia, femur-to-fibula and tibia-to-calcaneus penetration depth plus the penalty weight times the deviation of the mean knee-seat and ankle-seat distances from the baseline (seat vertices: the 200 tibia vertices nearest each partner)

effectiveRotationCentre.note: each frame's body motion B(f) B(1)^-1 is a screw motion; this solves its axis and reports how far that axis sits from the standing knee-seat centroid, plus how far the motion slides along its own axis. A constant pivot shift moves every frame's centre by the same vector, so it cannot follow an axis that wanders or a real translation

limitations: every configuration returns constants: a pivot shift can follow the flexion angle, but nothing here fits a joint centre per frame, adds cartilage or models contact
the fibula shares the tibia body frame, so it can only receive the same correction
the search scores a strided subset of frames; the reported figures are recomputed on all 101 frames
the seat penalties use one arbitrary weight and 200 nearest vertices each; the reported per-part figures should be read instead of the cost alone
penetration is measured between rigid vertex meshes with no cartilage, so a small residual contact may be anatomical rather than an error
one subject, right side, standing bounding-box registration, 101 frames of one squat
